findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its underlying storage/snapshots hold data in cleartext with no KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing MySQL to untrusted networks and greatly increasing attack surface for credential brute-force or exploit attempts. The public endpoint is also exported via the db_endpoint output.
The master username is the predictable default 'admin', which aids credential-guessing attacks against a publicly reachable database.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so access relies solely on a static master password with no centrally managed, rotatable IAM credentials.

The user_data script interpolates var.password and the DB username directly into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF-capable web app on the host and is stored unencrypted, leaking the database master password.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume containing the database credentials file is stored unencrypted.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is set, leaving IMDSv1 enabled; combined with the PHP application on the host, an SSRF could retrieve the instance profile credentials for the highly privileged ec2role.
The instance is placed in a public subnet and its public DNS name is exported as an output, exposing the unhardened HTTP application (served over cleartext HTTP, no TLS) to the internet.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance role. Any compromise of the internet-facing web instance yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 and RDS resources in the account, including privilege-escalation paths via ec2:RunInstances with other roles.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, permitting unconstrained outbound traffic and easing data exfiltration or C2 communication from a compromised resource.

The security group has no description and, combined with publicly_accessible = true on the attached RDS instance, the VPC-scoped ingress rule does not prevent internet exposure of the database endpoint.
